text.intro:
The question was which VIBES settings to use for new work: the solver, the rank and tau. Each step below asks one
question, shows the measurement and states the choice. EC is in µg per filter. Unless a figure says the calibration was rebuilt, EC is
read with the frozen k 4 IMPROVE model, which was trained on spectra corrected at rank 70 and tau 0.1.
text.solver:
VIBES first fits a noise level for each scan, then the baseline. In the October run the optimiser stopped within 30
steps on 155 scans (99 PM2.5, 14 PM10, 42 field blanks),
leaving the noise level too high and the baseline too close to the average blank. The converged solver fits the same objective until it
cannot improve. The scans here are the PM2.5 scans saved under the 87-blank background. A flatter corrected spectrum is shown for the
Addis early stops (3 Nov tests); that their lower EC is more correct is not shown.
text.rank:
The rank was lowered by keeping the first components of the rank-70 background, not by building a new background at each
rank. Rank 40 changes EC by a median 0.01 % and at most 0.03 µg, so components 41 to 70 do nothing to EC.
The 10 Nov injection test explains why: a band up to 150 cm⁻¹ wide survives at every rank on a loaded filter.
text.tau_fixed:
These numbers are the cost of correcting a spectrum one way and calibrating another. They do not say which tau is
best. The fitted noise level follows tau (median 3.1, 6.1 and 11.8 ×10⁻⁴ at tau 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2), so a noise
level only compares between fits made at one tau.
text.tau_refit:
IMPROVE (12,393 spectra) and Addis were corrected at each tau and each tau was scored with its own model. At
tau 0.1 the rebuild returns the 3 Nov calibration. Scores are compared at a fixed k. Of 12 comparisons with tau 0.1, tau 0.05 has a larger
error in 3 and a smaller one in 0; tau 0.2 has a larger error in 3 and a smaller one in 4. The intervals
resample sites 2,000 times.
text.krule:
The frozen procedure draws a site-grouped cross-validation curve on the train split and takes the first major minimum. That
rule picks k 4, 11, 4 at tau 0.1, 0.05 and 0.2. With one QC-failed spectrum left out of training it picks 4, 8, 3. The held-out RMSE
at k 4 is about 3.87 µg and at k 11 about 3.24 µg at every tau, so a setting judged at the rule's k is mostly being judged on k.
text.qc:
IMPROVE filter 2008808 (TONT1) is marked as failing raw QC in the decision bundle, and it is in the
train split of the frozen k 4 model. Its corrected spectrum is 364 times farther from the mean than a typical train spectrum.
The k 4 model was fitted with and without it on the converged tau 0.1 spectra and both were applied to the converged network run. The
model with it is the 3 Nov rebuilt k 4 model. IMPROVE cannot tell the two apart (held-out RMSE 3.850 against 3.873 µg),
but on SPARTAN PM2.5 scans EC moves by a median 17.2 %, 64.0 % of scans move by more than 10 %, and
Addis moves 5.3 %. Nothing here says which model is right: blanks read closer to zero without the
spectrum, repeat scans agree less well, and the Addis slope against HIPS is the same. The 3 Nov transfer table was made with the
spectrum in training; the scoring harness now leaves it out.
text.domain:
No network PM2.5 scan reads above 50 µg, and 1.5 % read above 25 µg, so the heaviest training
filters lie outside SPARTAN's range. Six training sets were tried: every QC-passed train spectrum, only those with thermal EC below 150,
100, 50 and 25 µg, and the 99 % of spectra nearest the mean. Each model was refitted with one of its six most extreme spectra dropped,
and on IMPROVE sites drawn with replacement 30 times. Trimming removes the pull of single spectra (6.1 % with everything in,
0.4 % below 25 µg). It does not pin EC down: with sites resampled a scan's EC still spreads by 7.6 % below 25 µg
(7.0 % at k 8, 6.6 % at k 12), and the models differ from each other by 3 to 30 %. The Addis slope against HIPS
goes from 0.41 to 0.23 at k 4.

The earlier finding that the Addis slope follows k was reread with the training set held fixed. It holds: under every one of the six
sets the slope rises with k, from 0.23 to 0.55 at k 4 to 0.81 to 2.11 at k 18. The training set moves it as well. Below 25 µg
the slope is 0.38 to 0.56 of the slope with every spectrum in, at every k, and it never reaches 1. From k 2 up, cut-offs of 150 and 100 µg stay
inside the band that resampling IMPROVE sites draws around "all" (0.29 to 0.61 at k 4, 1.16 to 1.72 at k 12). How closely FTIR EC
follows HIPS barely changes (R² 0.58 to 0.78 from k 3 up), so R² cannot choose between them: k and the training set set the scale of Addis EC, not its
pattern.
text.choices:
The solver, the rank and tau are settled by this work. The calibration is not. The number of PLS components moves
held-out accuracy far more than any of the three settings, and moves the Addis comparison with HIPS the other way. And at k 4 one training
spectrum changes SPARTAN EC by more than the solver, the rank and tau together.

meaning: The baseline method. It fits the part of a spectrum that a blank filter explains and subtracts it; what is left is the corrected spectrum.
How closely VIBES lets the baseline follow one spectrum. It is fitted for every scan before the baseline.
The routine that fits the noise level. The October run used one that sometimes stopped early; the converged solver runs until the fit cannot improve.
How many patterns of the blank background the baseline may use, largest first.
The quantile the baseline aims for under the spectrum. A lower tau puts the baseline lower.
The number of PLS components in the EC calibration, which reads EC from the corrected spectrum.
The IMPROVE EC calibration at k 4, trained on spectra corrected at rank 70 and tau 0.1. EC from it is only valid at those settings.

question: Does solving to convergence change EC?
Does the number of background components matter?
What happens if tau changes and the calibration does not?
Is another tau more accurate?
Does the rule that picks k give a stable answer?
Does a QC-failed training spectrum matter?
Is a model trained without the heaviest filters stable?
What do we do?
did: October run against converged on 3,626 PM2.5 scans
Every scan refitted at ranks 10, 20, 40 and 70 (4,376 of 4,376 certified at every setting)
Every scan refitted at tau 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2, EC read with the frozen model
IMPROVE calibration rebuilt at each tau (12,393 spectra), scored on held-out filters at fixed k
The frozen selection rule run at each tau, with and without one bad spectrum
The k 4 model fitted with and without IMPROVE filter 2008808 (TONT1), both applied to every network scan
Six training sets, from every QC-passed spectrum down to thermal EC below 25 µg; each refitted with one spectrum dropped and with IMPROVE sites resampled
found: Unchanged on 3,529 scans. The 97 early stops move by a median 5.1 %, Addis by 11.4 %
Rank 40 gives the same EC as rank 70 (median 0.01 %). Rank 20 moves it 0.5 %, rank 10 3.0 %
EC moves by a median 1.2 % at tau 0.05 and 2.0 % at tau 0.2
No tau is better at every k: tau 0.05 is never better, and worse at k 11 and 18; tau 0.2 is better at k 4 and 8 and worse at k 11 and 18
It picks k 4, 11, 4 at tau 0.1, 0.05, 0.2, and 4, 8, 3 without the bad spectrum
IMPROVE scores stay the same, but SPARTAN EC from the k 4 model moves by a median 17.2 %, and site medians by -64 % to +51 %

One spectrum stops mattering (6.1 % to 0.4 %), but EC still spreads 7.6 % when sites are resampled, and the cut-off itself moves EC by 3 to 30 %. The Addis slope against HIPS rises with k under every training set, and below 25 µg it is about half the slope at every k
The solver, rank and tau are settled. What moves EC is the calibration: its k and its training spectra
choice: Do not mix: tau must match the calibration
Compare settings at a fixed k
Leave it out; EC at k 4 is not pinned down by IMPROVE scores
Steadier, not pinned down; the cut-off is a choice, and so is k

check: Addis slope of FTIR EC on HIPS BC

why: Same objective, never a worse fit, all scans fit. EC is unchanged except on the 97 early stops
Rank 40 gives the same EC, so nothing is gained by lowering it, and field blanks are tightest at 70 (spread 0.003 µg against 0.022 at rank 20)
No tau is better at every k once the calibration is rebuilt; the largest gap between tau values at one k (4, 8, 11, 18) is 0.15 µg
It opens on rank 70, tau 0.1, converged. No other setting has evidence behind it
The selection rule picks a different k when tau changes (4, 11, 4), so a comparison at the rule's k compares k, not the setting

It is 364 times farther from the mean spectrum than a typical train spectrum. IMPROVE held-out RMSE is 3.850 with it and 3.873 without, but SPARTAN PM2.5 EC moves by a median 17.2 % and field blanks read 0.30 µg instead of 1.27
Two k 4 models that IMPROVE cannot tell apart differ by a median 17.2 % on SPARTAN. With IMPROVE sites resampled, a scan's EC spreads by 13.9 % and a site's median by 10.8 % (PRFJ 61 %)

No network scan reads above 50 µg and 1.5 % read above 25 µg, so the heaviest training filters lie outside SPARTAN's range. Training below 25 µg removes the pull of single spectra and lowers held-out RMSE on light filters from 3.04 to 2.66 µg, but it moves network EC by 17.7 %, Addis's median from 8.1 to 5.9 µg, and the Addis slope against HIPS to about half at every k. Nothing here says the lower reading is more correct

Held-out RMSE falls from 3.87 µg at k 4 to 3.24 at k 11, but the Addis slope against HIPS rises from 0.43 to 1.79 at k 18. IMPROVE accuracy and the Addis transfer pull in opposite directions. The slope rises with k under every training set, but the k where it reaches 1 depends on the set: k 9 with every spectrum, k 11 below 50 µg, never below 25 µg
A feature about 1,500 cm⁻¹ wide is removed at every rank (10 Nov check), so the continuum loss belongs to the background, not to rank or tau
